instructions: Crack the 4 eggs into a large bowl and add the 2/3 cup sugar and 2 tbsp honey. Whisk hard for about 3 minutes, until the mixture is pale, thick and falls from the whisk in a ribbon.
Sift the 1 1/3 cups flour and 1 tsp baking powder over the eggs. Fold them in with a spatula until there are no dry streaks left.
Cover the bowl and put it in the fridge for 30 minutes. The batter turns smoother as it rests.
Stir 1 tbsp water into the batter. It should pour like pancake batter. If it's still thick, add up to 1 tbsp more water.
Set a large nonstick skillet over the lowest heat for 5 minutes so it heats evenly, then turn it up to medium-low.
Dip a folded paper towel in the oil and wipe the pan with it, so there's only a thin shine and no beads of oil. Keep the oily towel by the stove.
Pour 3 tbsp batter from a few inches above the pan so it spreads into a round about 3 inches across. If your pan is big enough, cook two at a time.
Cook for 60 to 90 seconds, until bubbles cover the top. Flip it and cook the other side for 20 to 30 seconds, until the edges look dry.
Transfer the pancake to a plate, smooth golden side up, and lay a damp kitchen towel over it so it stays soft.
Wipe the pan with the oily towel and cook the rest of the batter the same way. That should be 12 pancakes, enough for 6 dorayaki.
Spoon a sixth of the red bean paste, about 3 oz, onto the pale side of a pancake, mounding it in the middle so it's thicker there than at the edges.
Set a second pancake on top, golden side up, and press the edges gently together. Make the rest the same way. This makes 6 dorayaki.
Wrap each one in plastic wrap so it holds its shape and stays soft. They keep at room temperature for up to 2 days.
method_notes: All three versions whisk eggs with sugar and honey until thick, fold in flour with a leavener, rest the batter, then cook small rounds in a barely oiled pan until bubbles show, flip briefly and sandwich two around sweet red bean paste. Just One Cookbook (the lead) uses all-purpose flour and baking powder; Cooking with Dog and RecipeTin Japan use baking soda dissolved in water, and RecipeTin Japan adds a little mirin. This one follows the lead and makes its full batch of 6 dorayaki from one 18 oz package of paste. The 30 minute rest is counted in the prep time.
